candidates.lesson_subject: IPS engine update lifecycle, memory-conserve thresholds, and inspection fail-open behavior
candidates.scenario_relation: Direct scenario: FortiOS 7.6.8 IPS Engine 7.01200 memory growth and conserve-mode transitions; Fortinet Community reports resolution in IPS Engine 7.01204.
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FDN-delivered IPS engine packages are separate from FortiOS firmware; IPS engine processes flow-based/NGFW traffic. Engine resource growth can cross red/green/extreme memory thresholds; IPS fail-open controls whether new flow-inspected sessions are dropped or passed unscanned.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate receives an IPS engine update from FDN -> ipsengine processes new flows -> memory crosses red threshold -> conserve mode changes inspection behavior -> TAC-supported engine package remediation.
candidates.failure_class: IPS-engine version regression or resource exhaustion causing conserve mode and reduced inspection / dropped sessions.
candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys top-mem 20 shows ipsengine as dominant memory consumers; diagnose hardware sysinfo conserve reports mode, used/freeable RAM and red/green/extreme thresholds; get system performance status shows utilization; diagnose debug crashlog read records conserve transitions. High ipsengine memory is correlation, not by itself proof of a leak or root cause.
candidates.remediation_path: Correlate FortiOS build and IPS engine version; preserve top-mem, performance and crashlog evidence; open Fortinet Support case for the corrected engine (the cited 7.6.8 incident was resolved in IPS Engine 7.01204); use only TAC-distributed manual packages. If a package upload fails with database error, temporarily enable diagnose autoupdate downgrade, upload the support package, then disable the setting. Do not lower conserve thresholds as a substitute for fixing the engine.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Diagnose ipsengine memory growth and repeated conserve transitions after a FortiOS upgrade; select supported engine remediation without silently bypassing inspection.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FDN update path into IPS engine plus RAM threshold state machine and fail-open/drop branches.

candidates.lesson_subject: Pinning and rolling back FortiGuard object-package versions served by FortiManager
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager local FDS serves a selected To Be Deployed Version per FortiGuard object package; Just Set Preferred Version freezes future package delivery without downgrading devices; Downgrade immediately rolls devices back; 20 object versions retained.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiManager receives packages -> administrator selects preferred version -> FortiGate update request is served with pinned package -> optional downgrade changes existing device package.
candidates.failure_class: Uncontrolled signature/object-package drift or unintended package rollback / update freeze.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Receive Status shows current package and To Be Deployed Version; device package version table shows whether device is already newer; FortiManager local FDS role confirms it is the server. A pin does not roll back FortiOS firmware and does not prove the device has installed a package until device state confirms it.
candidates.remediation_path: Select the specific package rather than changing all packages; test on a small device group; use Just Set Preferred Version to stop newer delivery without rolling devices back, or Downgrade only with explicit approval; check 20-version retention and update-server reachability; document how to restore Latest.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Select the package pin action that stops future signature updates but does not immediately downgrade a device already on a later package.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGuard package catalogue -> preferred-version decision -> hold or rollback device branch.

candidates.lesson_subject: Geo-redundant active-active HA over routed Layer 3 networks
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Active-active FortiAnalyzer HA lets each member receive logs/archive from directly connected devices and forward to peer and remote server; unicast heartbeat and VRRP 112 traverse L3; cluster VIP requires L2; at least one initial-sync-disabled node is required during formation.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure peers and group -> elect primary with initial-sync rule -> establish unicast heartbeat/VRRP -> each member ingests local logs and replicates to peer -> FortiGate server/alt-server failover.
candidates.failure_class: HA formation stuck in initial synchronization, heartbeat/peer failure across routers, or mistaken reliance on an L2 VIP in a routed design.
candidates.evidence_pattern: System Settings > HA role and peer state; FortiAnalyzer HA status; firewall permits VRRP 112 and unicast heartbeat; FortiGate config log fortianalyzer setting shows server/alt-server/fallback-to-primary. A healthy heartbeat alone does not prove each FortiGate forwards to the intended member or that archive data is fully synchronized.
candidates.remediation_path: Disable Initial Sync on at least one node during initial formation; verify group ID/name/password, peer IP and serial numbers; enable unicast heartbeat; permit VRRP 112; omit VIP across L3 and use the peer heartbeat interface; configure reachable server/alt-server addresses and validate log arrival from devices at each site.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Build an active-active HA pair across routed data centers with no shared VLAN; choose heartbeat, VIP, and initial-sync settings.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two routed sites with local log ingestion, unicast heartbeat/VRRP control and inter-node replication.

candidates.lesson_subject: Media Redundancy Protocol ring roles, election, VLAN requirements, and failure signaling
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: MRP ring uses one automanager and client nodes; ring ports are physical or one static trunk and excluded from STP; election chooses lowest numeric priority then lowest MAC; MRP_Test, LinkChange and TopologyChange frames signal ring state; MRP VLAN/domain must match.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure VLAN on both ring ports -> apply profile -> configure manager/client role and domain -> manager sends tests -> link failure/recovery produces state frames -> ring reconverges.
candidates.failure_class: Ring disabled or unstable due VLAN/domain mismatch, conflicting manager roles, STP interaction, unsupported MIM/MIC, or overly aggressive custom timers.
candidates.evidence_pattern: get switch mrp settings shows configured role/domain/VLAN/ports/profile; diagnose switch mrp status 1|2 shows live state; diagnose switch mrp stats shows counters; show switch mrp settings/profile verifies effective config. A configured ring does not prove all physical links are up or that the selected model supports MRP.
candidates.remediation_path: Check model feature matrix; ensure MRP VLAN is allowed/native on both ring ports; align domain ID/VLAN/profile across nodes; choose one automanager election model (do not mix manual manager and automanager); keep default 500ms profile until stable; avoid low test intervals that cause flapping; verify ring port state and STP exclusion.
candidates.question_fingerprint: MRP is disabled after VLAN changes; identify the mismatch between MRP vlan-id and ring-port allowed/native VLAN before changing election priority.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Closed MRP ring with elected automanager, client nodes, test frames and topology-change path.

candidates.lesson_subject: Layer 3 inter-controller roaming for bridge-mode SSIDs using direct or indirect handoff
candidates.scenario_relation: Adjacent intra-controller bridge-mode roaming across AP-group VLANs; used only to contrast with the primary inter-controller mobility-tunnel/direct-handoff feature.
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Different FortiGate controllers preserve client IP across VLAN/subnets using inter-controller mobility; bridge-mode roaming offers indirect controller tunnel or direct AP-to-AP mode without NAT; same SSID/security/passphrase and RADIUS dynamic VLAN assignment; idle timeout triggers DHCP rehome.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client roams to second controller -> traffic remains anchored via mobility tunnel or direct AP path -> client retains old IP -> idle timer triggers rehome and DHCP on destination subnet.
candidates.failure_class: Roaming breaks across controller boundary due peer/tunnel reachability, mismatched SSID/security, RADIUS VLAN assignment, NAT in direct mode, or premature/late rehome expectation.
candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c ha shows L3 roaming peer UP; diagnose wireless-controller wlac -d sta online shows client MAC/IP and l3r state on each controller; compare AP/controller/VLAN/IP before and after roam; packet capture checks direct AP path or controller mobility tunnel. A peer UP state alone does not prove client roam or DHCP rehome.
candidates.remediation_path: Use identical SSID/security/passphrase on both controllers; configure reciprocal peer IPs and l3-roaming enable; choose indirect unless direct AP reachability without NAT is proven; configure RADIUS dynamic VLAN attributes; set and test client-idle-rehome-timeout; correlate client monitor, DHCP, and mobility tunnel state.
candidates.question_fingerprint: A client roams across controllers and keeps its old IP; determine whether the mobility anchor is active or DHCP rehome has failed using peer and l3r state.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two controllers/APs/subnets with direct vs indirect handoff and timed rehome.

candidates.lesson_subject: Reusable CLI configurations with DO/UNDO lifecycle and port/host variable substitution
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC sends reusable CLI DO/UNDO command sets verbatim to switches/routers; no syntax validation; disconnect triggers UNDO; port/host variable matrix supplies %port%, %vlan%, %ip%, %mac%; invoked by model configuration, roles, access policies or scheduled tasks.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Control state changes -> policy selects command set -> variables substituted -> DO pushed -> disconnect invokes UNDO -> CLI task and port-change events record outcome.
candidates.failure_class: Device command syntax rejected, unsupported vendor command, stale state, variable substitution failure, or missing/incorrect UNDO causing residual network state.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Show CLI displays DO and UNDO text; In Use shows role/policy/scheduled-task references; Host/Port CLI Task Success/Failure and Port CLI Data Substitution Success/Failure events distinguish execution from substitution; Port Changes records when config was applied. A success event does not validate the intended data-plane ACL effect.
candidates.remediation_path: Test each command on the target device console first; group devices with common CLI syntax; build paired DO/UNDO sets; respect variable matrix (%vlan% not available in host-based UNDO); bind to a specific control-state/policy and validate Port Changes plus actual switch configuration.
candidates.question_fingerprint: A quarantined endpoint's port ACL remains after disconnect; identify the missing inverse action and variable-scope error.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC state/policy engine -> variable substitution -> DO command to switch; disconnect event -> UNDO return path.

candidates.lesson_subject: Local RADIUS certificate identity extraction and attribute-ranking precedence for EAP-TLS
candidates.scenario_relation: Materially updated Nov 4; PEAP-MS-CHAPv2 cached-credential failure after Windows KB5127648 is an adjacent EAP-method scenario. It explicitly states client-certificate authentication is unaffected; it is not evidence about certificate attribute ranking.
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F Local RADIUS can extract host/user identity from certificate CN and SAN fields (UPN, DNS, email) with configurable ranking; Client Certificate Attribute must be enabled to use non-CN values; UPN may need to be populated by the client; allow-spaces controls CN/SAN whitespace. This is identity mapping, not certificate trust/revocation.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Supplicant presents EAP-TLS client cert -> Local RADIUS validates TLS/trust -> reads candidate identity fields -> ranking chooses first available attribute -> Authentication Source maps identity -> RADIUS authorization/VLAN decision.
candidates.failure_class: EAP-TLS authentication succeeds at TLS layer but identity mapping selects wrong/empty CN/SAN value, producing unknown host/user or wrong authorization.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Local Server Client Certificate Attribute setting and ranking order; inspect certificate with openssl x509 -in client.pem -noout -subject -ext subjectAltName; compare CN, SAN-UPN, SAN-DNS and SAN-email to the identity recorded by Local RADIUS. TLS success does not prove the intended identity field was selected.
candidates.remediation_path: Enable Client Certificate Attribute when non-CN identity is required; populate the desired SAN (UPN/DNS/email) on the certificate; set ranking deliberately; permit spaces only if required; test machine and user certificates separately and verify the resulting identity before changing VLAN policy.
candidates.question_fingerprint: TLS succeeds but the endpoint maps to the computer CN instead of the intended SAN-UPN; select the required option and ranking correction.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Certificate with CN and three SAN attributes -> configurable priority ladder -> chosen identity -> auth source and RADIUS policy.

candidates.lesson_subject: RADIUS CHAP/MS-CHAPv2 compatibility with local-user password storage cryptography
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Administrator/sponsor local users always use irreversible bcrypt; regular user accounts use bcrypt when enhanced cryptography is enabled and reversible AES256 when disabled. PAP can validate local/remote accounts; CHAP/MS-CHAPv2 supplies a hash response and requires eligible local reversible storage; remote LDAP passwords stay at LDAP.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: RADIUS client selects PAP or CHAP/MS-CHAPv2 -> FAC resolves account source/role -> storage algorithm is checked -> method-specific verification -> Access-Accept/Reject.
candidates.failure_class: Authentication-method/password-storage mismatch or attempting CHAP/MS-CHAPv2 with remote LDAP, administrator, sponsor, or bcrypt-only accounts.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Authentication method configured on NAS/RADIUS client; FAC user role and Enhanced cryptography for storage of local user passwords setting; local/remote user type; RADIUS debug shows method and user lookup result. A successful PAP test does not prove CHAP/MS-CHAPv2 will work because the password-storage requirements differ.
candidates.remediation_path: Map each RADIUS client to an authentication method supported by the account source; use PAP only where the RADIUS transport/security design permits it; if CHAP/MS-CHAPv2 is mandatory, use eligible local user accounts with reversible AES256 storage and understand the security trade-off; do not expect administrator/sponsor or remote LDAP accounts to satisfy that requirement.
candidates.question_fingerprint: PAP succeeds but MS-CHAPv2 fails for a local user after enhanced storage was enabled; identify the password-storage incompatibility.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: PAP vs CHAP paths through local/remote source and bcrypt/AES256 storage gates.

candidates.lesson_subject: Role-based separation of secret metadata from decrypted credential and audit-log access
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM roles separate Secret List/Folder access from viewing decrypted passwords/passphrases/SSH keys. View Encrypted Information requires Secret List Read/Write; View Secret Log gates edit history/activity/SSH filter logs. Folder/root-folder permissions are independent of decrypted-value permission.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Role assigned to user -> folder and secret metadata permissions allow record access -> Secret List Read/Write plus View Encrypted Information gate clear credential display -> View Secret Log separately gates audit tabs.
candidates.failure_class: Over-privileged role exposes decrypted credentials; under-privileged role blocks legitimate viewing; audit logs are hidden because the dependent View Secret Log permission is absent.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Role definition shows each permission; Secret List and folder permissions; test account sees metadata but receives 'User accprofile doesn't allow access to clear sensitive information' for password; log tabs appear only when View Secret Log is enabled. UI visibility does not prove a user can launch a secret target.
candidates.remediation_path: Create a custom least-privilege role instead of modifying protected defaults; grant Secret List read/write only where required; disable View Encrypted Information for metadata-only operators; grant View Secret Log only to auditors who need it; test with a non-admin account and inspect audit trail.
candidates.question_fingerprint: An operator can view a secret record but must not reveal its password; choose the least-privilege role settings and explain the Secret List prerequisite.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Role matrix with independent folder/metadata, decrypted-value and audit-log gates; dependency arrow from Secret List to clear credential.

candidates.lesson_subject: Microsoft Entra ID ingestion through Azure Event Hub plus Generic HTTPS Poller for risky users
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Entra Audit/Sign-in/Provisioning/Device/Group/Policy/Role/Graph events arrive via Azure Event Hub; Risky User Status uses a separate Generic HTTPS Poller against Graph API. Event type prefixes identify each family; initial event arrival can take about 15 minutes and in some cases up to 24 hours.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Entra diagnostics -> Event Hub -> FortiSIEM event ingestion; separate app registration/client ID/tenant ID/secret -> Graph riskyUsers API -> Generic HTTPS Poller -> risk-state events.
candidates.failure_class: Partial identity telemetry because Event Hub categories, shared access policy, tenant/app permissions, poller credentials, or client-secret lifecycle are misconfigured.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Search Resources > Event Types by MS-Entra-* prefixes; inspect Event Hub incoming messages and consumer connection; verify app registration tenant/client IDs, consent and secret validity; distinguish initial ingestion delay from a broken poller. Seeing audit events does not prove Risky User Status collection works because it is a separate poller.
candidates.remediation_path: Configure Event Hub and FortiSIEM ingestion independently from the Graph poller; enable required Entra diagnostic categories; use the correct Event Hub policy; grant required API permissions/admin consent; store and rotate client secret before expiry; verify each event family by its prefix and allow for Azure forwarding latency.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Audit and sign-in events arrive but risky-user state is absent; identify the independent Graph poller credential path.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two independent telemetry lanes: Event Hub streaming and Graph API poller.

candidates.lesson_subject: MSSP tenant isolation across FortiCloud OUs, FortiCare accounts, ADOMs, SPA licensing, and ZTNA sync
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE is single-tenant with one instance per FortiCare account/customer child OU; FortiSASE license belongs to child account. SPA hub entitlement is checked in same/root account; FortiManager connector is same/root account with one connection per ADOM; ZTNA telemetry uses EMS Access Key independent of OU hierarchy.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: MSSP root OU -> child OU/FortiCare account -> register one SASE instance/license -> map to dedicated FMG ADOM -> verify hub SPA license -> establish SPA and separate EMS-key ZTNA telemetry sync.
candidates.failure_class: Tenant isolation/integration failure caused by license registered to wrong account, missing hub SPA entitlement, FortiManager connector outside allowed account hierarchy, ADOM mismatch, or assuming SASE instance itself is multi-tenant.
candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiCloud OU/account hierarchy; FortiCare registration and FortiSASE license placement; hub SPA license count and FortiSASE SPA control state; FortiManager ADOM-to-SASE connector mapping; EMS Access Key and telemetry sync status. Successful SPA does not prove ZTNA telemetry sync, which uses a separate credential path.
candidates.remediation_path: Create a dedicated child OU/FortiCare account per customer and register one SASE instance there; place the SPA-licensed hub in same/root account; put FortiManager in same/root account and map one connection per ADOM; configure ZTNA telemetry separately with FortiCloudEMS Access Key; validate tags and policy boundaries per tenant.
candidates.question_fingerprint: A SASE tenant is licensed but SPA is locked while FMG connector works; identify the separate hub entitlement and account-scope dependency.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: MSSP root OU with customer child OUs, one SASE per account, shared root FMG ADOM slices and root multi-VDOM SPA hub.

candidates.lesson_subject: FortiCloud Overlay-as-a-Service configuration transaction, licensing, and rollback control plane
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: OaaS is a FortiCloud subscription wizard for regional SD-WAN overlay; each participating FortiGate requires OaaS entitlement. OaaS agent uses FGFM to compare/validate desired FortiOS config and apply it transactionally; failure rolls back all orchestrated changes. ADVPN is an underlying shortcut dependency, not the lesson focus.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate registers/activates -> OaaS controller sends desired config over FGFM -> agent validates and commits transaction -> status/version/task ID reports outcome -> failure triggers rollback; operator corrects conflict and retries.
candidates.failure_class: OaaS entitlement missing/expired, device not online in FortiCloud, FGFM tunnel unavailable, unsupported FortiOS, configuration validation/apply failure, or rollback after partial orchestration.
candidates.evidence_pattern: System > FortiGuard shows OaaS license state; diagnose test update info includes SWOS entitlement; get oaas status shows account/site/configuration version/sync status/task ID/error; deployment task status shows controller outcome. OaaS license does not prove configuration sync succeeded; ADVPN shortcut presence does not prove OaaS agent transaction succeeded.
candidates.remediation_path: Confirm OaaS/Cloud Advanced entitlement on every participating FortiGate; ensure devices are powered, activated, logged into FortiCloud and FGFM reachable; confirm regional dual-hub topology and site online state; inspect get oaas status and task error; resolve config conflict and redeploy; rely on agent rollback for failed transaction and verify version before retry.
candidates.question_fingerprint: The portal shows a new overlay topology but the spoke still runs its old configuration; use OaaS status and license/FGFM evidence to distinguish desired state from committed transaction.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiCloud OaaS controller -> FGFM desired-config transaction -> validate/commit/rollback at FortiGate; ADVPN shown only as downstream dependency.
